course.title: Atomic – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 9

unit.title: Angles
unit.blurb: Angles with parallel lines and in triangles, interior and exterior angles of polygons, ruler-and-compass constructions and Pythagoras' theorem.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Calculate angles using angle facts: angles on a line, around a point, in a triangle, and alternate, corresponding and co-interior angles.

O2.t: Derive and use the sum of the interior angles of a polygon.

O3.t: Use the sum of exterior angles of a polygon (360°) to find angles and the number of sides of regular polygons.

O4.t: Describe and use ruler-and-compass constructions: perpendicular bisector, angle bisector and the perpendicular from a point to a line.

O5.t: Use Pythagoras' theorem to find a missing side of a right-angled triangle and solve problems.

p: Angles on a straight line add to **180°**; angles around a point add to **360°**; angles in a triangle add to **180°**.
With **parallel lines**: **alternate** angles (Z shape) are equal, **corresponding** angles (F shape) are equal, **co-interior** angles (C shape) add to 180°.

A triangle has angles 48° and 67°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.

p: A polygon with n sides can be split into **(n − 2) triangles** from one vertex, so the interior angles add to **(n − 2) × 180°**.
A **regular** polygon has equal angles, so each interior angle is **(n − 2) × 180° ÷ n**.

p: The number of triangles is n − 2, not n. A hexagon has 6 − 2 = 4 triangles, so its angle sum is 720°.

p: In a right-angled triangle the longest side, opposite the right angle, is the **hypotenuse** c. **a² + b² = c²**.
To find the hypotenuse: **add** the squares, then square-root. To find a shorter side: **subtract** the squares, then square-root.
